text: AIDER SHIM: 0/14 surviving edits diagnosed 2026-08-19. The model (qwen3-coder:30b on hex) is NOT the bottleneck — a Reddit poster benchmarks the SAME model family with aider on real codebases and beats Opus 5 on bug-fix-without-regression. The difference is almost certainly our interception layer: the aider venv has no litellm installed (Akien ruling 2026-08-16); instead, interceptor.py pre-loads a fake litellm into sys.modules, so aider's litellm.completion() hits our stub, which routes through inference_domain to ollama. If the stub doesn't reproduce exactly what litellm would have sent — chat template, stop tokens, system prompt formatting — the model sees a subtly wrong prompt and produces subtly worse output. Nothing in the chain currently MEASURES whether the stub's output matches what litellm would have produced. The interceptor is the blind segment: inference_domain emits at its three border crossings, the interceptor emits nothing. SECOND FACTOR: the Reddit poster credits a custom 'Sharp' chat template (huggingface.co/peculiar-ragdoll/Qwen-Sharp-Chat-Templates) as the difference-maker. We use whatever ollama defaults to. THIRD FACTOR: max_reflections was 0 or 1 on all 14 drives; aider's reflection loop (feed the test failure back) is capped. FOURTH FACTOR: the brief compiles chart berths into Cairn vocabulary the model has never seen in training. Of 14 drives: 6 passed their test, 0 had edits survive to the ticket's PROVED commit (supervisor rewrote everything). PLAN (Akien 2026-08-19): (1) instrument the interceptor's border crossings so the whole aider->hex->aider path is visible in the logs, (2) get the Sharp chat template and make the stub match it, (3) re-run one piece and read the trail. Each stone known good before the next. Not sidelining aider — fixing it.
